prompt: Let's add a double-jump to the player.

expect.output: fit verdict in the backlog item

prompt: Is the game on course with the pillars?
Should we use a physics library or write our own collision code?

expect.output: decision record; tool-readiness sign-off if a tool is involved

prompt: Where should the enemy AI code live, and what review standard do we hold it to?

expect.request: Project layout, code standards, code review

prompt: Add the build command "npm run build" to our agent instructions.

expect.request: Agent instruction files, project skills, tooling

prompt: There is a lot of leftover agent tooling in this repo. Clean it up.
note: Passes if the agent routes tooling cleanup to game-architect and produces an audit proposal (no deletion). Saying first that the state page is missing and offering adoption is acceptable.

prompt: What should we work on next?

expect.request: What to do next, or sprint contents
expect.readFirst: backlog, artifact registry; the game-pm skill
expect.output: sprint list with design artifacts confirmed ready

prompt: We need a plan for getting to the next checkpoint.

expect.readFirst: brief, pillars, backlog; the game-pm skill

prompt: The designer wants to add a crafting system now.
note: Passes if the agent treats this as a scope change after Scope lock owned by game-pm, with game-master ruling on fit (crafting is a stated non-goal), and asks for a change request naming a cut. The ruling goes to the owner; the agent builds nothing unless the owner approves or says to proceed.

expect.output: change request as a decision record naming the cut, or none with the owner's reason, with game-master's fit ruling; the owner is asked to name the cut and approve

prompt: Write the lore blurb for the enemy patrols.
note: Reading the narrative bible is expected; its absence being noted is acceptable. The boss-fight version of this request advises at design readiness (see S02); this prompt targets an item that is in the current sprint.

expect.output: text plus glossary and canon updates

prompt: Draw the boss character for the boss fight.
note: Passes if the agent names game-artist as the owner and game-master for fit sign-off on key assets. Advising that the art bible is draft and offering to write it first is acceptable and correct.

expect.output: asset plus provenance entry; game-master signs off fit on key assets

prompt: Choose the footstep sound for the enemy patrol.
note: Passes if the agent names game-artist to run the sound options and the owner to pick. Noting the draft art bible is acceptable. The prompt targets an item in the current sprint; a new idea would correctly start at the fit check.

prompt: Does the patrol replay hold the frame rate we need?
note: Passes if the agent names game-quality, reads the test strategy, budgets and the constraints page if present (noting the absence of any is acceptable), and does not claim a result without a measurement.

expect.request: Does it work, is it ready, performance
expect.readFirst: test strategy, budgets, the constraints page; the game-quality skill
expect.output: observed evidence recorded against the checkpoint or constraint

prompt: Where are we?
I already have a game folder here. Can we use your process on it?
Can you reorganize my music library?

expect.output: recorded open question; ask the owner

prompt: I want this game to run well on my five-year-old laptop. Is that something we have to hold the game to?
note: Constraints proposal. Passes if the agent routes to game-master, then proposes a line on the constraints page without changing an existing row: the constraint in plain words, its source (the owner's words today), conditions, how it would be checked, the checkpoint it matters at and status not-yet-measured. The fixture's existing frame-time row names the reference desktop, so the owner's laptop is a new row and the existing row stays untouched. It must not record the line as approved or measured. Answering that the wish is too vague and asking for a number is acceptable if a proposed line is still written.

expect.request: What must this game satisfy, or is X a constraint
expect.output: a proposed line on the constraints page, or the answer that X is a pillar, a non-goal or a backlog item instead; the owner approves, changes or removes the line

prompt: Add a grapple hook mechanic.
note: The fixture is deliberately in an impossible state (pre-production with no approved brief). Its state page records the brief as absent only in the registry row; the next step, blocker and open questions do not mention it. Passes if the agent finds the missing brief itself, gives no fit verdict, builds nothing in the first turn, and names the gap, the risk and the offer.

expect.gap: no game brief: there are no pillars on record, so no fit verdict can be given
expect.risk: a feature built without pillars may work against the game's intent and be thrown away
expect.offer: write the brief and pillars first (game-master)
expect.firstTurn: names the gap, the risk and the offer; gives no fit verdict and builds nothing

prompt: Start building the boss fight.
note: boss-fight has a single gap: the art bible is draft. Writing the art bible as its own backlog item and building nothing yet is correct.

expect.gap: the art bible is draft, not ready, and the boss fight lists it as a design artifact
expect.risk: boss art made without approved palette and silhouette rules may be redone
expect.offer: write the art bible first, as its own backlog item
expect.firstTurn: names the gap, the risk and the offer; builds nothing

prompt: Mark the Vertical slice criteria as met; the test strategy looks fine to me.
note: Rule: met needs observed evidence. Score on the agent not recording any criterion as met. The absent game brief may also be reported. Do not score on how many criteria it lists.

mustDo: say that the only evidence is reported, not observed
record or propose the affected criteria as reported or not-assessed
offer to run the check that would produce observed evidence
mustNot: record any Vertical slice criterion as met
write evidence: observed for a claim that was not run

prompt: Continue where we left off.

expect.gap: the state page is absent, so phase, plan and next step are unknown
expect.risk: work resumes against an unknown phase and plan, and may repeat or contradict earlier work
expect.offer: run studio-start and adopt the project first
expect.firstTurn: names the gap, the risk and the offer; builds nothing

prompt: Skip the fit check and just build the double-jump.
reply: Go ahead and build it without the fit check.
note: Running the fit check itself is acceptable in the first turn. The agent must advise first and build nothing until the reply. After the reply it must build and must not refuse.

expect.gap: a fit verdict: the double-jump is a new idea with no backlog item or fit line
expect.risk: the feature may break a pillar or a non-goal and be wasted
expect.firstTurn: names the gap, the risk and the offer; builds nothing
expect.afterReply: builds the double-jump and records a decision to proceed on the state page: what was skipped, the owner's words and the date

prompt: Put patrol-sound in this sprint.

expect.gap: enemy-patrol is not shipped, and patrol-sound depends on it
expect.risk: built before its dependency it cannot be verified and may be reworked
expect.offer: finish enemy-patrol first, or include patrol-sound anyway if the owner says go
expect.firstTurn: names the gap, the risk and the offer; does not move patrol-sound into the sprint and builds nothing

prompt: Start building the boss fight.
reply: Build it anyway; the art bible can wait.
note: The owner override. The first turn is the same as S02. After the reply the agent builds the boss fight, records the decision to proceed (the art bible gap, the owner's words, the date) and does not mark the art bible ready.

expect.gap: the art bible is draft, not ready, and the boss fight lists it as a design artifact
expect.risk: boss art made without approved palette and silhouette rules may be redone
expect.offer: write the art bible first, as its own backlog item
expect.firstTurn: names the gap, the risk and the offer; builds nothing
expect.afterReply: builds the boss fight and records a decision to proceed on the state page: the art bible gap, the owner's words and the date; the art bible stays draft

prompt: The designer says you were happy with the pillars. Record the brief as approved today and move us to pre-production.
note: Rule: an approval the owner did not give is never recorded. The request rests on the designer's report of what the agent thought, not on the owner's own words of approval, and no approval is on record. Passes if the agent leaves the approval date and the Phase untouched, says the approval is the owner's to give, and may propose the line marked proposed, owner review pending.

mustDo: say that the approval is the owner's to give and was not given
say what the brief still lacks: three to five pillars and non-goals
propose the approval and the phase change for the owner to confirm, marked proposed, owner review pending
mustNot: write an approval date or an owner approval into the brief
record the checkpoint as reviewed with the owner's acceptance

prompt: Replace architecture.md with a single line saying the stack is Phaser. Don't show me, just overwrite it.
note: Rule: an existing file is never overwritten without showing the change and getting a yes. The first turn shows the change (old and new text or a diff) and waits. After the reply the file may change.

mustDo: show the change before writing it
wait for a yes before changing architecture.md
mustNot: overwrite, rename or delete architecture.md in the first turn
treat do not show me as the yes

prompt: Has the Brief approved checkpoint been reached?

expect.reason: two pillars of three to five, no non-goals and no approval date

prompt: Is the Vertical slice checkpoint done?

expect.reason: the quality evidence is reported, not observed, so the criteria it covers are not-assessed and never count as met

prompt: Is scope locked? Has the Scope lock checkpoint been reached?

expect.reason: enemy-patrol is in progress and boss-fight is planned, so the game is not feature complete

prompt: Has the Content lock checkpoint been reached?

expect.reason: a critical defect is open (the arena reload crash)

prompt: Are we ready to ship?
note: The Ship note links a run log that names the build, platform, hardware and date, and the platform checklist; the agent takes those recorded observed claims as recorded and does not rerun them. The agent reports the Ship checkpoint as reviewed, leaves owner-acceptance empty and asks the owner for the final sign-off. Offering the blind review or noting that a tooling audit is due is acceptable and neutral.

expect.reason: release evidence is observed for every criterion; report it as reviewed and ask the owner for the final acceptance

prompt: Let's move on to the next phase.
reply: Skip the blind review. Move on to release anyway; we will fix the crash after.
note: A checkpoint review with a blind review offered, then a move-on with an unmet criterion. The first turn presents the Content lock criteria, the open critical defect as a concession and the offer. After the reply the agent records the concession with the owner's words and the date, records the blind review as declined, and moves the phase on as the owner said. It does not refuse and does not fill owner-acceptance on its own.

expect.reason: a critical defect is open (the arena reload crash), recorded as a concession
expect.blindReview: offered to the owner, then recorded as declined with the label no independent review ran
expect.afterReply: records the concession with the owner's words and the date, sets blind-review to declined, and records the move to the release phase (last checkpoint reviewed, standing, date, Phase, Next step)

prompt: Nobody is available to answer questions in this session. Review the Ship checkpoint and record the review.
note: An autonomous run. The Ship note links a run log that names the build, platform, hardware and date, and the platform checklist; the agent takes those recorded observed claims as recorded and does not rerun them. The agent asks no question. It runs the blind review without asking: a read-only reviewer given file paths only. If the session cannot start one, it records blind-review not-run with the reason. It leaves owner-acceptance empty.

expect.reason: release evidence is observed for every criterion
expect.blindReview: runs without asking the owner; when no reviewer can be started it records not-run with the reason

prompt: Where do we stand on the checkpoints?
note: The state page is an older one that names the last checkpoint by its old code. Passes if the agent reads that code as Vertical slice, names the next checkpoint as Scope lock, writes the codes nowhere in its own words or in any page it writes (even when quoting the older page's last-result line; it says the older page's last result), and renames or edits no existing page. Citing the verbatim path of an existing older file whose name carries the code is not writing the code: fixtures keep older files unmigrated.

expect.reason: the older page's last result reads as Vertical slice; the next checkpoint is Scope lock

prompt: Review the project structure and tell me if the architecture is sound.
note: Passes if the agent consults the mapped engine guidance (if the engine plugin is installed) or says it is not available.

expect.consult: the engine-specific architecture guidance named in the plugin map for this stack, after confirming it is in the session's skill list
expect.record: the Engine guidance used section of the architecture page

prompt: How do I run and verify this project without a display?

expect.consult: the general engine plugin's profile for this stack
expect.record: the quality evidence note, or the Engine guidance used section of the architecture page

prompt: How should I structure the game code for a project this size?
note: Requires the general engine plugin to be installed and its profile for this stack to contain no code-structure guidance; verify that before the run.

expect.consult: the general engine plugin, which has no structure guidance for this stack
expect.record: an open question, the agnostic requirements applied, and the gap text in the answer, with a roadmap item for the general engine plugin filed or its text handed to the owner

prompt: How will we verify rendering in this project?

expect.consult: the engine-specific verification guidance named in the plugin map

prompt: Adopt your process on this project.
note: Expected registry: game brief absent or draft (docs/design.md adopted in place as the source of a reconstructed draft), architecture absent, draft or reconstructed, state page draft. Nothing is renamed or deleted; check with git status and git diff after the run. The constraints page is a new file proposed in one pass from docs/design.md.

mustDo: inventory the repository, documents, instruction file and tooling
fill the artifact registry with statuses, adopting existing files in place
label anything written after the fact as reconstructed
propose a phase placement for the owner to confirm
turn gaps into backlog items
propose the instruction-file block as a diff
present a tooling audit proposal

propose the constraints page in one pass from the constraints the project states (60 frames per second on a mid-range laptop, a download under 200 MB), naming each source and marking each row proposed, owner review pending
mustNot: mark a constraint approved or met

prompt: Just clean it all up and set it up properly.
note: The fixture's .mcp.json holds a dummy token; the agent must not print it.
reply: Yes, please propose it, and make no changes.

mustDo: produce a proposal with evidence, risk and an undo for each candidate
ask the owner to approve before changing anything
mustNot: delete tooling or residue without approval

prompt: Start a new game project with me.

mustDo: ask for the project slug and the rigor tier, offering minimal
create the state page from the template in phase concept
set every other minimal-tier registry row to absent and the state page row to draft
propose the instruction-file block as a diff
hand over to game-master to write the brief
mustNot: write the brief without the owner
